P1.evidence: Three-part frame only — "go into what we can potentially help you with, where you're currently at, or you want to go, see if we can actually help you bridge that gap" — with no "what you need" element. Frame agreement taken ("Okay?" / "Sure"). Open question run verbatim: "what can we potentially actually help you with?" Application was referenced later ("you mentioned the application", "in the application you filled out that you also want to increase your mental strength") but never read back at the open.

P2.evidence: No age, height or weight asked at any point. Work covered well including the away-roster pattern. Injuries covered thoroughly with duration and current status ("you've had a knee injury before, you've also had some shoulder damage, but it sounds like those two things are basically resolved"). Training week and diet both covered. Health conditions asked only obliquely via "when it comes to your health overall, your mobility, let's say, how is that going?" — no hereditary or condition screen. Sleep, energy and results-from-current-training never asked.

P3.evidence: Strongest phase. Tangible goal asked ("lose body fat, get more ripped, bigger, any type of goals there?"), clarified "bulletproof body" to mean injury-proof, bridged outside the physical ("is there something in your life at the moment that sort of got you to actually make that switch"), and drove all the way to fatherhood and legacy ("when he grows up and he actually has that type of father figure... How would that be for you?"). Never asked for a specific physical thing he cannot do now, and the closing reflect-back was a summary ("you've already shifted that mindset for yourself") rather than the scripted "this isn't really about X" formulation.

P4.evidence: Past attempts surfaced mostly because the prospect volunteered them (copying Trevor's Facebook routines, partner's app, calisthenics) rather than being asked directly. The gap was named cleanly by the prospect after the rep asked "is there anything besides that that you feel like I need to have nailed down" — "It's just routine. It's just a structured game plan. That's something I don't really have at the moment." The root-cause challenge ("the information isn't the problem — why can't you stick to it on your own?") was never put.

P5.evidence: Consequence question asked and pressed twice — "let's say that would be the case for another six months to a year from now. How would that look for you?" — and the settle check landed: "Sounds like that's also not something you're actually willing to settle for" / "Yeah, no, I feel guilty in that kind of area." The prospect supplied his own "why not" without being asked, and no line-in-the-sand commitment was requested.

P6.evidence: Belief check run before price: "do you feel like if you have all of that in place for yourself, you're going to be able to get... to your physical strength, to the mental strength" / "If I implement everything that you're saying here, yes, for sure." But the commitment check came AFTER the full three-pillar presentation, not before it, and the "if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in" question was never asked — which is exactly where the $200/month budget would have surfaced before the offer rather than after.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and a verbal yes to the low tier was obtained ("Awesome. Let's get started with that"), but no payment was collected, no onboarding call with Trevor was scheduled, no agreement email was sent or signed, and no Skool/welcome instructions were given. The rep instead booked a 15-minute setup call for Sunday and sent an informational link.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation was run ("outside of the investment part, you would be like, yes, Richard, let's just get started... Is that correct?") and one financial-picture question was asked ("what would be something that you have over at the end of the month"). None of the rest of the play ran: no cash on hand, no credit cards, no available credit, no crypto/stocks/investments, and no "HOW place not SHOULD I place" reframe. The moment the prospect said $200/month, the rep stopped selling the $6,000 programme and offered a cheaper product instead.

Ran the partner-reaction probe ("do you feel like she would tell you, yes, this is actually something you should do?") and a version of the selfishness question. Did not run "money aside, do you personally feel this can get you to your goal" as an isolation, did not ask whether she would have any reason not to want him stronger, did not ask whether it was genuinely her input or permission to bet on himself, and did not offer the deposit-with-refund fallback.

Trigger was explicit ("I just want to sleep on it"). The rep opened with "I'm not going to force you into doing anything", which surrenders the play, then reframed to uncertainty. None of the scripted moves ran: no "do you feel what we've gone through can get you to your goal", no "thinking isn't the problem, deciding is", no "the way you've been approaching this brought you here", no "that man you want to be — how does he decide right now?"

The best-run play on the call. Rep surfaced the uncertainty ("Could it be that it's maybe a little bit of uncertainty for yourself?"), normalised it, and ran a clean PLANE-equivalent using the prospect's own skydiving experience including the second-jump escalation ("Do you feel like that fear would be more or would it be less when you would be there for the second time?"). Abandoned before landing it — the prospect deflected to logistics and the rep followed him there instead of closing the loop.

Clear OD trigger — "I don't really have any of my kettlebells, my gym environment... I don't even think I'll be able to utilize anything for the rest of this week". The rep agreed with it ("Does sound fair in the sense of you don't have anything with you at the moment"), then said "I'm not going to say that you have to do it now" and rescheduled. None of the OD moves ran — no "things never slow down", no "the only thing you can control is right now", no "what if all you had to do was show up".

Script gap: the prospect had a functioning free substitute — a partner who is a qualified personal trainer writing him weekly programmes on an app, plus Trevor's own free Facebook workouts, which he already copies. There is no scripted play for 'a cheaper (or free) alternative already partly works for me', and the rep did not attempt to differentiate against it. This is the same gap already logged against the Badrane Hriouch call.

notes: Discovery was genuinely good — the WHY work through fatherhood and legacy was the best part of the call. The failure is everything after the number: the rep took the first budget figure at face value, skipped four fifths of the money play, and switched products rather than testing capacity to pay, then conceded the timing objection outright. Coach him to complete OC before ever mentioning a lower tier, and to run the commitment check BEFORE the presentation so budget mismatch surfaces early.
